page: Microsoft Azure L32s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine driven by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor delivering 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. The hardware architecture incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Complementing the compute resources, the instance allocates 256.0 GB of system memory, representing a ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, and bundles 7679 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results show balanced compute output and strong memory-bound bandwidth. The server registers a Geekbench single-core score of 2147.0 and a multi-core score of 18442.0, both placing in the top 25 percent tier. Uncached memory read bandwidth over large 256 MB blocks reaches 197.62 GB/sec, supporting fast throughput for memory-intensive routines. The integrated AMX instructions and large memory pool also support high-throughput execution for small CPU-based language models, delivering 392.66 tokens/sec for text generation on 135M parameter models. However, execution speed slows considerably on 70B parameter models down to 2.78 tokens/sec due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware.

Cost efficiency is centered around dense local I/O and large RAM capacity on a single node. The bundled 7679 GB NVMe storage eliminates separate block storage attachment costs for data-heavy pipelines. While write bandwidth on large memory blocks is average at 86.34 GB/sec, decompression and static web serving throughput remain strong at 209.27 GB/sec and 56.27 GB/sec respectively. Microsoft Azure L32s_v4 is well suited for high-transaction relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, real-time analytics engines, and high-throughput data ingestion workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure L32s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 260 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX support. The system bundles 256.0 GB of memory alongside 7679 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory density without discrete GPUs. In synthetic testing, it achieves strong Geekbench scores of 2147.0 single-core and 18442.0 multi-core, as well as uncached large-block read bandwidth of 197.62 GB/sec. Static web throughput reaches 56.27 GB/sec, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression hits 209.27 GB/sec. This configuration offers solid resource density for transaction-heavy databases, NoSQL clusters, search indexing, and real-time big data pipelines requiring dense local NVMe storage.
